counterexample: Tutte's 46-vertex graph is finite, simple, cubic, planar, 3-connected, and has no Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary:
1. Let G be an arbitrary finite simple, cubic, planar, 3-connected graph. — Justified: this fixes an arbitrary graph satisfying the hypotheses.
2. Choose a cycle C of maximum length in G. — Justified: a finite graph of minimum degree 3 contains a cycle, and finiteness ensures that a longest one exists.
3. If C contains every vertex, then C is Hamiltonian; therefore suppose C is not spanning. — Justified: this is exactly the definition of a Hamiltonian cycle and a valid case reduction.
4. Let H be a component of G−V(C). Then H has at least three distinct neighbors on C. — Justified: one or two such neighbors would form a vertex cut of size at most two separating H from the remaining vertices, contrary to 3-connectivity.
5. Choose consecutive attachment vertices x and y of H on C. Since H is connected, there is an x–y path P whose internal vertices lie in H. — Justified: paths from x and y into the connected component H can be joined, and a simple subpath may be selected.
6. Let A and B be the two x–y arcs of C. Both P∪A and P∪B are cycles. — Justified: P meets C only at x and y, so adjoining either arc produces a simple cycle.
7. Claim that planarity, cubicity, and the presence of at least three attachments allow x,y and P to be chosen so that |P|>|A| or |P|>|B|. — Not justified: none of the stated hypotheses gives this length inequality. Indeed, maximality of C implies the opposite inequalities |P|≤|A| and |P|≤|B| for every such P, since otherwise Step 6 would already produce a longer cycle. This is the first failing step.
8. If |P|>|A|, replace A by P (and similarly for B) to obtain a cycle longer than C. — Conditionally justified from the asserted inequality, but unusable because Step 7 was not established.
9. This contradicts the maximality of C. — Conditionally justified from Step 8, but no contradiction has actually been derived because Step 7 fails.
10. Therefore C must be spanning. — Not justified: it depends on the unproved contradiction.
11. Hence every 3-connected cubic planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. — Not justified: the attempted proof has failed.
12. The statement is in fact false: Tutte's 46-vertex graph satisfies all the stated hypotheses but has no Hamiltonian cycle. — Justified: it is a standard explicit counterexample to the claimed universal statement.
